headline: G2 GOLDFIELDS SHAREHOLDERS VOTE 80.6% TO APPROVE C$3B G MINING DEAL — GUYANA GOLD HUB HEADS TO ONTARIO COURT FOR JULY CLOSE
snippet: G2 Goldfields shareholders voted 80.61% in favour at a June 16 special meeting to approve the C$3 billion all-share arrangement with G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN), with 208.5 million shares — 80.61% of the total — represented at the meeting. Each G2 share will receive 0.212 GMIN shares at an implied price of C$10.84 per share, a 72% premium to the 30-day VWAP. Separately, G2 will spin out G3 Goldfields with C$45 million cash (C$30M from G2 treasury plus C$15M from GMIN) to hold non-core exploration properties outside the arrangement. The deal closes in July 2026 pending Ontario Superior Court of Justice approval. The acquisition consolidates G Mining's Oko West mine with G2's adjacent Oko deposit in Guyana's Puruni greenstone belt — creating a multi-million-ounce production corridor. For TSX junior gold investors, the 80.6% vote on a deal announced only 67 days prior (April 10) and a 72% acquisition premium confirm that the M&A bid for high-quality Guyana gold assets at current $4,300+ gold prices is real, not speculative.

headline: ENERGY FUELS' WHITE MESA MILL HITS 1.6M LBS U3O8 BY JUNE 30 — FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE ACHIEVED IN 6 MONTHS AT $9–12/LB
source_name: Metal Tech News / Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU) expects its White Mesa Mill in Utah to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of U3O8 by June 30, 2026 — hitting the low end of its full-year guidance of 1.5 to 2.5 million pounds in just six months. Processing costs at the mill are running at historic lows of $9–$12 per pound of U3O8. The current ore processing campaign is expected to complete by end of June to rebuild stockpiles from the Pinyon Plain and La Sal conventional uranium mines; a second processing campaign is planned for Q4 2026, subject to market conditions and a potential rare earth element processing campaign. At uranium spot $86/lb and long-term contracts at $91.50/lb — with U.S. utilities accelerating contracting ahead of the January 2028 ban on Russian-origin uranium imports — completing annual guidance in six months at sub-$12/lb cash costs establishes White Mesa as the most capital-efficient licensed conventional uranium mill in the Western world, with REE processing optionality at the same facility providing a second value driver ahead of Q3.

headline: LUMINA METALS +19% ON WARSAW DEBUT — POLAND FLOATS "COPPER VALLEY" VISION AS NOWA SOL PROJECT ADVANCES TOWARD EU COPPER HUB
snippet: Lumina Metals Corp. (TSX: LMCU; WSE: LMCU) commenced trading on the Warsaw Stock Exchange on June 16, 2026, with shares surging 19% to 35.5 zlotys (C$13.53) as Polish retail investors gained first access. Poland's government simultaneously floated a "Copper Valley" concept positioning the country as a European copper production hub. Lumina raised C$406.2 million in its April 2026 TSX IPO (which tripled its original target) to advance the Nowa Sól copper-silver project in southwestern Poland, which could more than double Poland's national copper output alongside KGHM — currently among the world's top ten copper producers. At COMEX copper near $6.42/lb and the U.S. Commerce Secretary facing a June 30 deadline to deliver a refined copper tariff assessment to President Trump, the Lumina WSE dual-listing provides European institutional access to a tier-1 EU copper project at a moment when Western copper supply chain security has become a political priority on both sides of the Atlantic.

headline: GOLDSILVER: SILVER OUTLOOK JUNE 2026 — THE CORRECTION FROM $89 WAS THE SETUP, NOT THE TOP
snippet: GoldSilver.com's June 2026 silver outlook, published June 16, reframes the pullback from the May peak (~$85–$89/oz) as a structural accumulation window rather than a cycle reversal — arguing that the six-year cumulative supply deficit exceeding 800 million ounces, the US-Iran ceasefire removing the energy-CPI headwind, and the FOMC June 17 rate hold together form the three-part foundation for silver's next leg higher. At $70+ silver and a gold:silver ratio of 61.7, the analysis notes that a compression toward bull-cycle historical averages of 45–50:1 would place silver at $87–$96 at current gold levels. The article identifies the May-to-June 2026 consolidation as the accumulation phase preceding Q3 catalysts: dot-plot resolution, Zijin's Manono lithium commissioning (adding industrial silver demand context), and potential Iran deal formalization. For retail silver mining investors, the GoldSilver framework frames the June pre-FOMC pullback below $70 as the recurrent pattern that defines the best entry windows in the current structural bull cycle.

headline: F3 URANIUM DEPLOYS 3D-DCIP AT TETRA ZONE — THREE-PROPERTY PLN SUMMER PROGRAM TARGETS FRESH ATHABASCA BASIN DISCOVERIES
source_name: Junior Mining Network / F3 Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FUU)
snippet: F3 Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FUU) launched its 2026 summer exploration program on June 16 at the Patterson Lake North Project in the western Athabasca Basin, advancing new target areas across three properties — Patterson Lake North, Minto, and Broach — while deploying a 3D-DCIP and resistivity geophysical survey over the JR Zone's Tetra conductor. F3's approach uses geophysical refinement to rank basement conductors by uranium-hosting probability ahead of drilling, the same workflow that generated NexGen's Arrow discovery and IsoEnergy's Larocque East system. At uranium spot $86/lb and long-term contract prices at $91.50/lb — with utilities accelerating contracting ahead of the January 2028 US-Russia import ban — a summer program that systematically ranks multiple targets across three western basin properties positions F3 to enter the fall drill season with its highest-quality conductor prioritisation since the original JR Zone discovery.

headline: BIG RIDGE GOLD SPUDS HOPE BROOK 2026 — INFILL + STEP-OUT + 2,000m GEOTECHNICAL AT NEWFOUNDLAND PAST PRODUCER
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Big Ridge Gold Corp. (TSXV: BRAU)
snippet: Big Ridge Gold Corp. (TSXV: BRAU) commenced its 2026 drill program at the Hope Brook Gold Project on June 16, targeting infill and step-out drilling at the 240 Zone and Main Zone on the southwest coast of Newfoundland, alongside approximately 2,000 metres of geotechnical and hydrogeological drilling. Hope Brook is a past-producing gold deposit on the Trans-Canada access corridor; the inclusion of a dedicated geotechnical drill component — covering pit wall stability and water management — signals that the company has advanced beyond pure resource drilling toward the engineering studies that precede a Preliminary Economic Assessment. For TSXV junior gold investors, a simultaneous infill/step-out plus geotechnical drill program at a past-producing Atlantic Canada gold project at $4,300+ gold marks the project-lifecycle transition that typically expands the acquirer pool from junior-focused buyers to mid-tier producers seeking near-development assets in low-risk, infrastructure-accessible Canadian jurisdictions.

headline: WARSH'S FOMC DEBUT: RATE HOLD CERTAIN, DOT PLOT IS THE REAL BINARY FOR GOLD AND SILVER THIS AFTERNOON
snippet: Kevin Warsh chairs his inaugural Federal Open Market Committee meeting June 16–17, with a rate hold at 3.50–3.75% priced at 97.4% probability — but the Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot) and Warsh's 2:30 PM ET press conference on June 17 are where gold and silver actually trade. The pivotal question: does the median dot still project a December 2026 hike, or does Warsh signal neutrality now that the US-Iran ceasefire has deflated the energy-CPI risk premium that drove May's 4.2% inflation read? If Warsh frames the energy surge as geopolitical-transitory rather than structural, real yield expectations compress and gold's technical recovery from the June seven-month low at $4,165 accelerates through the $4,338–$4,347 resistance zone. If the dot plot is unchanged, the 70% December-hike probability that markets currently price remains the binding constraint on the precious metals complex into Q3. For junior mining investors, Warsh's debut represents the single largest forward-rate catalyst event of the second half of 2026.

headline: FXSTREET: GOLD VOLUME REVERSAL AT LOWS — $4,242 BREAKOUT TRIGGER CLEARED, NEXT RESISTANCE AT $4,560 ENTERING FOMC WEEK
snippet: FXStreet's June 14 technical analysis identified a volume reversal pattern at gold's seven-month lows — the same structure that preceded the metal's three largest rallies in the current 2024–2026 bull cycle — with $4,242 as the key breakout trigger. That trigger has since been cleared as the Iran-US ceasefire catalysed a move to $4,309–$4,347, shifting the intermediate-term picture from corrective to impulsive ahead of Wednesday's FOMC press conference. The next meaningful resistance cluster sits at $4,560–$4,600, where the prior consolidation stalled. The volume reversal at lows is analytically significant because it reflects buyer exhaustion from institutional sellers, not continued downside pressure; when sellers run out of stock at a floor anchored by central bank demand at $4,150–$4,218, recoveries tend to be sharp and sustained. For junior mining investors using gold technicals as a position-sizing guide, the cleared $4,242 trigger and $4,560 next resistance provide a concrete technical framework for sizing through Warsh's 2:30 PM ET press conference on June 17.

headline: CANADIAN MINING REPORT: GOLD MINERS PRICED AT $3,100 GOLD WHILE SPOT TRADES AT $4,300 — ANALYSTS SEE MAJOR VALUATION CATCH-UP AHEAD
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's June 2026 analysis documents a persistent valuation gap in gold equities: senior producer NAV multiples currently imply gold at $3,100–$3,400, not the $4,300 spot price, meaning equity markets have not yet priced the metal at current levels — let alone institutional year-end targets of Goldman Sachs $5,400, JPMorgan ~$6,000, Morgan Stanley $5,200, or UBS $5,500. The analysis notes that Q1 2026 earnings confirmed record gross margins for senior producers, and that ongoing M&A — with Agnico Eagle's Finnish consolidation and G Mining's Guyana consolidation both closing near simultaneously — is systematically removing the sector's cheapest assets first, raising the valuation floor for remaining undisturbed juniors. The classic case for junior gold equities over physical: a 30% gold price increase at $1,200/oz cash costs on a $4,300 gold price implies roughly 2x operating leverage on margins, meaning junior producers and advanced developers with strong resource bases should outperform physical gold if institutional year-end targets are approached. For retail investors building junior mining positions during the current June consolidation, the persistent valuation lag is the setup that top analysts are referencing as the primary entry argument.
